[Source PDF page 8]
(Option B, question 5 continued)
The temperature data is downloaded every day and collated into a master file.
The data from the master file is loaded into a suitable array for that 24-hour period.
The following statistics are calculated:
y Maximum temperature
y Minimum temperature
y Mean temperature
As Nauru is very close to the equator, the length of the day changes very little throughout
the year. For the purposes of part (f), the lengths of its day and night are:
y Day: 07:00 to 18:59 inclusive (12 hours)
y Night: 19:00 to 06:59 inclusive (12 hours)
(f) Construct a pseudocode algorithm to calculate the:
y maximum temperature
y minimum temperature
y mean temperature
y mean night-time temperature.
Assume the arrays for the time of day of the reading and hourly temperature readings
have already been set up and populated as parallel 1D arrays. [8]

source_issues: SRC-043 PDF p14 uses a cross-midnight condition TIME >= 19:00 AND TIME < 07:00, which is impossible, and inconsistent NIGHT_TOTAL/TOTAL_NIGHT names. The adapted hour-based answer uses OR and counts the included observations before division; boundary, negative and constant-value cases are tested.
